class.name: MidiInput
class.brief_description: Reads a MIDI input port (a keyboard, a controller, another program) and plays it through a [MidiDriver], or hands it to scripts.
class.description: A node: add it to the tree, [method open] a port from [method get_ports], and either connect [signal received] or [method set_driver] to play what arrives on that driver's channel targets. [codeblock] var input := MidiInput.new() add_child(input) input.open(MidiInput.get_ports()[0].id) input.set_driver(midi) # live notes play on midi's instruments input.latency_ms = 20.0 # optional: exact spacing for a fixed delay [/codeblock] Messages arrive on the platform's MIDI thread with their arrival time and are handed out on the main thread every frame. Played through a driver, a live note is that driver's like any other: its [method MidiDriver.stop] and [method MidiDriver.panic] end it. Values arrive as MIDI 1.0 (the ports speak it) and reach the driver's targets at MIDI 2.0 resolution, as everything does. Platforms: ALSA on Linux (loaded at run time: without it there are no ports), CoreMIDI on macOS, WinMM on Windows. Android has no ports yet. SysEx and system messages reach [signal raw_received] only.

method.name: close
method.description: Closes the port. Nothing arrives after this returns.

method.name: get_driver
method.description: The driver live messages are played on, or [code]null[/code].

method.name: get_open_error
method.description: Why the last [method open] failed, or an empty string.

method.name: get_port_id
method.description: The open port's id, or an empty string.

method.name: get_ports
method.description: Every MIDI input the platform offers, as a [Dictionary] each with [code]id[/code] (what [method open] takes, stable while the port exists) and [code]name[/code]. Empty where the platform has no MIDI system.

method.name: inject_bytes
method.description: Handles [param bytes], one whole MIDI 1.0 message, as if it had just arrived: for tests, and for MIDI from elsewhere (a network, a custom device).

method.name: open
method.description: Opens the input with this id (see [method get_ports]), closing any open one. Returns [code]false[/code], with the reason in [method get_open_error], if it cannot.

method.name: set_driver
method.description: Plays what arrives on [param driver]'s channel targets ([code]null[/code] for none). Channel messages only: notes, controllers, pitch bend, pressures and programs.

members.member: 0 (the default): each message plays as soon as possible, so up to a frame late, unevenly. Above 0: each plays exactly that long after it arrived, so the spacing of what was played is kept, at the cost of that fixed delay. 10-20 ms suits most playing.

signal.name: raw_received
signal.description: Any message arrived, as its bytes: SysEx, clock and transport messages included.

signal.name: received
signal.description: A channel message arrived: [param kind] a [enum MidiDriver.EventKind] (a note-on with velocity 0 comes as a note-off), [param channel] 1-16, [param index] the note or controller, [param value] in MIDI 1.0's range (pitch bend -8192 to 8191), [param time_us] when it arrived, on [method MidiDriver.get_time_us]'s clock.
